# Lecture 16 — Source Verification Audit

**Lecture:** Part 16 (final in the uploaded series) — *A Guide To Islamic Child Raising (Tarbiyah)*, Shaykh Usama Abdulghani (Light of Guidance).
**Video:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTGFDLPB6Vk (1:03:01)
**Transcript basis:** YouTube auto-generated English captions. Arabic phrases and Persian names are heavily garbled; reconstructions below are marked as such.
**Audit date:** 2 September 2026. **Method:** primary Arabic text + reference where obtainable; chain and named grader where one exists; explicit "NOT LOCATED" where not.
**Shared index:** items already settled in `_verified-index.md` are cited, not re-researched.

*(Sections are written in order of the lecture; the headline findings sit at the top and were written last.)*

## Headline findings

- **This is the best-sourced lecture in the series so far, and that should be said plainly.** Six citations are strongly verified against primary Imami collections with correct Imam, correct wording and correct sense: the souls of the believers in the barzakh (**al-Kafi 3:248**), *amarani rabbi bi-mudarati'l-nas* (**al-Kafi 2:117**), the three tests of the Shia (**al-Khisal p.103 h.62**), Imam al-Baqir's "they are not the Shia", the *makarim al-akhlaq* triad (**Wasa'il 15:200**), and Imam al-Kazim with the farmer (**Maqatil al-Talibiyyin 499-500**, cross-attested in *Tarikh Baghdad*). Both Qur'anic references he gives by number — **36:12** and **36:30** — are **correct**, and **al-Mizan supports the exact use he makes of both**.
- **⭐ One clear factual error, and it is on the story he tells at greatest length.** In the two-loaves narrative the recall messenger is said to come "**from Imam Sadiq**." ❌ In the source (*Muntaha al-Amal* 2:38-39) the story is **Imam al-Sajjad's from beginning to end** — he weeps, he sends the loaves, and **he** sends the messenger. There is no Imam al-Sadiq in it.
- **⭐ The Imam al-Kazim story is real and better than he tells it.** Verified to *Maqatil al-Talibiyyin* pp. 499-500 and *Tarikh Baghdad* 13:28, including "which was better, what you wanted or what I wanted?". ⚠ But the man hoped for **200** dinars and the Imam gave **300** — the Imam gave **more than the man hoped for**, which is a stronger point than the speaker's flattened "he hoped 300, got 300." And the line "Allah gives us *rizq* based on what we hope for" is **not in the source**.
- **The index's recurring flags recur.** (1) The **righteous child as best legacy** — in the Imami three-legacies text the child is **third**; ⭐ **use al-Kafi 7:57 instead**, «ستة تلحق المؤمن بعد وفاته», which contains his own improvised list of wells and charity *and* puts the child first. (2) **"Islam began as a stranger" is Sahih Muslim 145 — Sunni-canonical, with no Imami primary located.** That is now the fourth or fifth time a *sahih* Sunni text has been given to a Shia audience as "the hadith tells us" without saying so.
- **Roughly half the *karamah* material is chainless maxim corpus and is never labelled as such.** Nine items here — the litmus test, *salamat al-din wa'l-dunya*, *man hajara'l-mudarat*, *al-karim yara makarima af'alihi*, *al-karim yabtahiju bi-fadlih*, *man kathura imtinanuhu*, *'ajibtu li-rajulin*, the *makarim al-akhlaq* continuation, and Imam al-Husayn on *hawa'ij* — come from *Ghurar al-Hikam*, *'Uyun al-Hikam*, *Mustadrak al-Wasa'il* or Bihar's *mawa'iz*, none of which carries an isnad. They are corroborative, not probative. **He also splices two of them** (N15 + N16) into one narration.
- **All three martyrs are correctly identified; none of the three anecdotes could be verified.** Mohammad Boroujerdi (b.1955, killed by a landmine on the Mahabad–Naqadeh road, 22 May 1983), Tahereh Hashemi (martyr of the Amol uprising, Jan 1982) and Mehdi Bakeri (b.1954, Operation Badr, 16 Mar 1985, 31st Ashura Division, body never recovered) are all real, correctly named, correctly aged. ⚠ **Every Iranian-hosted source carrying their memoir anecdotes was 403- or robots-blocked at the egress proxy this session** — so "not verified" here means *unreachable archive*, not *refuted*.

## Quranic verses

The speaker cites three verses. **All three are cited accurately** — including the one the ear expects him to get wrong.

### 36:12 — "and We write what they have sent ahead and their traces"
**Verse.** ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا وَآثَارَهُمْ ۚ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾
**Translation** (Ali Quli Qarai): "Indeed it is We who revive the dead and write what they have sent ahead and their effects [that they left behind], and We have figured everything in a manifest Imam."
**Context.** Surah Ya-Sin, in the opening address to the Prophet about those who will and will not be warned.
**Tafsir al-Mizan** (Arabic retrieved). Tabataba'i glosses *atharuhum* exactly as the speaker uses it — as what a person leaves behind for after his death: «ما تركوها لما بعد موتهم من خير يعمل به كتعليم علم ينتفع به أو بناء مسجد يصلى فيه أو ميضاة» ("what they left for after their death of good that is acted upon — such as teaching knowledge that benefits, or building a mosque prayed in, or an ablution facility"). He notes the same applies to bad legacies left behind. His *bahth riwa'i* on the verse cites the *sunnah hasana* hadith (Jarir b. 'Abdullah al-Bajali): «من سن سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها من بعده… ومن سن سنة سيئة…».
**Verdict.** ✅ **Correct verse, correct reference, and the tafsir supports the exact use he makes of it** (continuing reward in the barzakh from good left behind). One of the cleanest citations in the whole series.
**Confidence.** Strongly verified.

### 36:30 — "no messenger came to them but they mocked him"
**Verse.** ﴿يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚ مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾
**Translation** (Qarai): "How regrettable of the servants! There did not come to them any apostle but that they used to deride him."
**Context.** The close of the parable of the town and the believing man of Ya-Sin; the *hasrah* is the regret over the servants' derision, not the martyr's own speech.
**Tafsir al-Mizan** (Arabic retrieved). Tabataba'i holds the exclamation to be **God's own speech**, not the murdered believer's, and reads the vocative form as intensifying: «أي يا ندامة العباد، ونداء الحسرة عليهم أبلغ من إثباتها لهم». He treats the mocking as a standing habit of the deniers across generations, not an isolated event.
**Verdict.** ✅ **The reference is correct.** The content he quotes ("no messenger came except that they mocked him") is indeed 36:30 and he cited it as 36:30. (Cognate verses with the same clause are **15:11** — *wa ma ya'tihim min rasulin illa kanu bihi yastahzi'un*, of the earlier communities — and **43:7**. His choice of 36:30 is the right one for the wording he gave.)
**Confidence.** Strongly verified.

### 2:83 — "and speak good to the people"
**Verse.** ﴿…وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا…﴾ — part of the covenant taken from Bani Isra'il.
**Translation** (Qarai): "…and speak kindly to people…"
**Context.** ⚠ The speaker quotes the clause with **no reference at all** and applies it directly to Muslims dealing with non-Muslims. The verse's addressee in its own context is **Bani Isra'il**; the extension to Muslims is an application, not the plain sense. (Compare the index entry on 2:85, where the same speaker's generalisation from Bani Isra'il to Muslims was flagged.)
**Tafsir al-Mizan** (Arabic retrieved). ⭐ **al-Mizan actually supports his application.** Tabataba'i takes *husna* as «مصدر بمعنى الصفة جيء به للمبالغة», i.e. «والمعنى قولوا للناس قولاً حسناً», and then says the phrase is «كناية عن **حسن المعاشرة مع الناس، كافرهم ومؤمنهم**» — "an idiom for good social conduct with people, their disbeliever and their believer alike." That is precisely the two-tier reading the speaker attributes to Imam al-Sadiq. In the *bahth riwa'i* he cites al-Kafi from Imam al-Sadiq: «قولوا للناس، ولا تقولوا إلا خيراً حتى تعلموا ما هو».
**Verdict.** ✅ Verse and wording correct; the universal-scope reading is **al-Mizan's own**, so the speaker is on solid ground even though he gave no citation. ⚠ He should say the surah and verse number aloud — a parent cannot look up an unreferenced quotation.
**Confidence.** Strongly verified (verse and tafsir); the specific al-Sadiq narration he paraphrases is treated separately below (N7).

## Narrations

### N1. The dead rejoice at *istighfar* "as the living rejoices at a gift" — [01:38]
**Arabic.** «إنَّ المَيِّتَ لَيَفْرَحُ بِالتَّرَحُّمِ عَلَيْهِ وَالاسْتِغْفَارِ لَهُ كَمَا يَفْرَحُ الحَيُّ بِالهَدِيَّةِ»
**Translation.** "The dead person rejoices at mercy being sought for him and forgiveness being asked for him, just as the living person rejoices at a gift."
**Reference.** Circulates in the late compilations; **Bihar al-Anwar 79:62** (chapter material on the barzakh and on connecting with the dead) is the citation most commonly given. Shaykh Habib al-Kadhimi and Jam'iyyat al-Ma'arif reproduce it introduced by **«رُوِيَ»** ("it has been narrated") — i.e. without an Imam named and without an isnad in the source that carries it.
**Chain.** None. It reaches us *mursal*.
**Authenticity.** Ungradeable. No assessor has graded it because there is no chain to grade.
**Confidence.** **Moderately verified** — the wording is stable and widely reproduced, the reference is not securely pinned to a primary collection.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ Accurate rendering; he even gets the Arabic clause *kama yafrahu'l-hayyu bi'l-hadiyya* right. ⚠ He calls it "the hadith tell us," which is fair, but a listener should know it is a chainless report.
**Practical meaning.** The point survives the weak chain because it is corroborated by much stronger material — see N2.

### N2. ⭐ Six things that follow the believer after death — the better citation the speaker did not use
**Arabic.** «سِتَّةٌ تَلْحَقُ المُؤْمِنَ بَعْدَ وَفَاتِهِ: وَلَدٌ يَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُ، وَمُصْحَفٌ يُخَلِّفُهُ، وَغَرْسٌ يَغْرِسُهُ، وَقَلِيبٌ يَحْفِرُهُ، وَصَدَقَةٌ يُجْرِيهَا، وَسُنَّةٌ يُؤْخَذُ بِهَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ»
**Translation.** "Six things reach the believer after his death: a child who asks forgiveness for him, a *mushaf* he leaves behind, a tree he plants, a well he digs, a running charity, and a practice taken up after him."
**Reference.** **al-Kafi 7:57**, Kitab al-Wasaya (cited as such by Jam'iyyat al-Ma'arif, *silat al-mayyit*).
**Confidence.** Moderately verified (reference confirmed in a secondary citation; no chain grading retrieved).
**Verdict.** ⭐ **This is the narration his whole opening segment wants.** He improvises the list — "we could be building schools, we could be building wells" — and then reaches for the *legacy* hadith. The al-Kafi text already contains the wells, the running charity, the practice taken up after him, **and** the child who does *istighfar*, and in this version the child is **first**. Recommend as a substitute; see also N3.

### N3. "The best thing a person leaves behind is a righteous child who asks forgiveness for him" — [05:43]
**Reference.** ⚠ Already settled in `_verified-index.md`: the **three legacies** narration — *sadaqa jariya / sunnat hudan / walad salih* — Bihar 71:257 from Imam al-Sadiq, with the Sunni parallel **Muslim 1631 (sahih)**. **In that narration the righteous child is THIRD, not first**, and the speaker made the same slip in earlier lectures.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ⚠ **Repeat error, though a milder one here.** He does not enumerate the three this time; he simply asserts that the *best* legacy is the righteous child. That ranking is not in the Imami text he is drawing on. It IS the order in the **Sunni** version at **Ibn Majah, *Sunan*, "خير ما يخلف الرجل من بعده ثلاث: ولد صالح يدعو له…"**, where the child comes first — but he does not cite Ibn Majah, and in the Shia recension the child is not singled out as best. The honest formulation is "**among** the best things."
**Confidence.** Strongly verified (as a correction).

### N4. ⭐ Where the souls of the believers are — [02:39]
**Arabic.** «أَرْوَاحُ المُؤْمِنِينَ فِي حُجُرَاتٍ فِي الجَنَّةِ، يَأْكُلُونَ مِنْ طَعَامِهَا وَيَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ شَرَابِهَا وَيَتَزَاوَرُونَ فِيهَا»
**Translation.** "The souls of the believers are in chambers in the Garden; they eat of its food and drink of its drink and visit one another in it."
**Reference.** **al-Kafi 3:248**, Kitab al-Jana'iz, in the chapter on where the souls of believers and disbelievers go after death — narrated by **Abu Basir** from **Imam al-Sadiq**. The longer wording with *wa yatazawaruna fiha* is in **al-Barqi, *al-Mahasin* 1:238**, from Imam al-Sadiq via Ibrahim b. Ishaq. Companion texts in the same al-Kafi chapter: 3:249 (Yunus b. Zabyan) and 3:250-251 (Durays al-Kunasi ← al-Baqir, the believers' souls in a garden eating its fruits).
**Chain.** Abu Basir ← Imam al-Sadiq (al-Kafi); the *Mahasin* version has its own chain.
**Authenticity.** No published rijal verdict retrieved for this specific hadith. The chapter as a whole is standard, oft-cited barzakh material with multiple independent narrators — Abu Basir, Yunus b. Zabyan, Durays — which is itself corroborative.
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified** as to text and reference; **needs further verification** as to grading.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Correct Imam (al-Sadiq), correct question ("where are the souls of the believers?"), correct Arabic, correct content** — chambers, eating, drinking, mutual visiting. This is the best-executed citation in the lecture and it is exactly the material a parent can use with a child.
**Practical meaning.** ⚠ One caution. He adds that the dead "can see their place in paradise, and for this reason they make du'a that Allah bring it sooner." That element is not in the text quoted above; it belongs to a different narration family. Say the two separately.

### N5. The Prophet forbidding one to pray for death — [02:39]
**Status.** ⚠ **Sunni-canonical, Imami parallel not located in this audit.** The famous wording is «لَا يَتَمَنَّيَنَّ أَحَدُكُمُ المَوْتَ لِضُرٍّ نَزَلَ بِهِ» — Bukhari 5671 / Muslim 2680, with the continuation "and if he must, let him say: O Allah, keep me alive so long as life is better for me…" (**sahih**, Sunni). Budget: one search; no Imami primary located.
**Verdict.** ✅ **The content of his claim is correct** — the Prophet did forbid wishing for death. ⚠ He presents it as a general Islamic teaching without a source; a listener should know the strongest text for it is in the Sunni *sihah*, and the point is not that death is undesirable but that one must not wish it *out of distress*. That qualification matters here, because his whole point is that a child should find death sweet.
**Confidence.** NOT LOCATED (limited search) on the Imami side; strongly verified on the Sunni side.

### N6. "Allah is Karim and loves generosity" — [07:44]
**Arabic.** «إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَرِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الكَرَمَ، وَيُحِبُّ مَعَالِيَ الأَخْلَاقِ وَيَكْرَهُ سَفْسَافَهَا»
**Translation.** "Allah is generous and loves generosity; He loves lofty character and hates its debased forms."
**Reference.** Prophetic. Narrator **Sahl b. Sa'd**. Graded ***sahih bi-shawahidihi*** ("authentic by its corroborants") by **Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut**, *Takhrij Sharh al-Sunna* 12/322, with supporting chains in al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi. It also circulates in the Imami maxim compilations (Rayshahri, *Mizan al-Hikmah*, s.v. *al-karam*, h.17) attributed to the Prophet.
**Authenticity.** **Sahih by corroboration — al-Arna'ut named.** ⚠ The grading is a **Sunni** one; no Imami chain-grading located.
**Confidence.** Strongly verified.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ Accurate, and he quotes the useful half. ⚠ He drops the second clause — *and He loves lofty character and hates its debased forms* — which is the half that turns the hadith into a parenting instruction rather than a slogan.

### N7. ⭐ "My Lord commanded me to be tolerant with people as He commanded me to perform the obligatory acts" — [26:01]
**Arabic.** «أَمَرَنِي رَبِّي بِمُدَارَاةِ النَّاسِ كَمَا أَمَرَنِي بِأَدَاءِ الفَرَائِضِ»
**Translation.** "My Lord commanded me to deal with people with *mudara* just as He commanded me to discharge the obligatory duties."
**Reference.** **al-Kafi 2:117**, Kitab al-Iman wa'l-Kufr, *bab al-mudara* — the Prophet, reported through Imam al-Sadiq. Also **al-Saduq, *Ma'ani al-Akhbar***, and reproduced in Bihar's *bab al-taqiyya wa'l-mudara* (73). Citation to al-Kafi 2:117 independently confirmed in Jam'iyyat al-Ma'arif al-Islamiyya's own *Mudarat al-Nas* — i.e. the speaker's own curriculum gives this exact page.
**Chain.** al-Kafi's chapter chain; no rijal verdict retrieved in this audit.
**Authenticity.** **Needs further verification** as to grading; the text is beyond doubt as to existence and wording, attested in two independent 4th-century collections (al-Kulayni and al-Saduq).
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified** (text and reference); grading unretrieved.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Correct and correctly deployed.** He renders it almost exactly and draws the right inference: *mudara* is not a concession to weakness but sits alongside the *fara'id*. This is the load-bearing hadith of his *mudara* section and it holds up.
**Practical meaning.** *Mudara* in the Imami lexicon is amicable dealing with people **short of compromising religion** — it is the sibling of *taqiyya mudaratiyya*, which is why it lives in Bihar's *taqiyya* chapter. Note the corollary he does not mention: the same chapter's «رأس العقل بعد الإيمان بالله مداراة الناس **في غير ترك حقّ**» (Bihar 74:145) — "*without abandoning a right*."

### N8. "Whoever abandons *mudara* has misfortune as his companion" — [24:00]
**Arabic.** «مَنْ هَجَرَ المُدَارَاةَ قَارَنَهُ المَكْرُوهُ»
**Translation.** "Whoever forsakes forbearance, the disagreeable becomes his constant companion."
**Reference.** Circulates among the **short maxims of Imam al-Jawad** (al-Jawad's *kalimat* as collected in Bihar vol. 75 and reproduced in the popular anthologies). ⚠ No primary-collection reference could be pinned within the search budget.
**Chain.** None. Maxim corpus.
**Authenticity.** Chainless and ungradeable, like *Ghurar* / *'Uyun al-Hikam*.
**Confidence.** **Moderately verified** — wording stable and correctly quoted; attribution to Imam al-Jawad rather than the generic "hadith" the speaker gives.
**Verdict.** ✅ Wording accurate. ⚠ Cite it as Imam al-Jawad and as a chainless maxim, not as "hadith" full stop.

### N9. "The safety of religion and world lies in *mudara* with people" — [32:05]
**Arabic.** «سَلَامَةُ الدِّينِ وَالدُّنْيَا فِي مُدَارَاةِ النَّاسِ»
**Reference.** **Imam Ali, *Ghurar al-Hikam wa Durar al-Kalim*** (al-Amidi) — indexed in the *mudara* cluster (entries incl. 1313, 4629, 5252, 5610).
**Authenticity.** **Chainless — *Ghurar* carries no isnad at all** and is therefore ungradeable. See the standing note in `_verified-index.md`.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified (located, ungradeable).
**Verdict.** ✅ Wording correct, attribution to the Ahlul Bayt corpus correct. ⚠ It is a maxim, not a transmitted *hadith* with a chain — and the speaker's framing ("so one of them hadith now it says…") does not distinguish. Corroborative, not probative.

### N10. Imam Ali's litmus test of the *karim* — [11:48]
**Arabic.** «مَنْ لَمْ يُجَازِ الإِسَاءَةَ بِالإِحْسَانِ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ الكِرَامِ»
**Translation.** "Whoever does not requite mistreatment with kindness is not one of the noble."
**Reference.** Imam Ali, ***Ghurar al-Hikam*** (Rayshahri, *Mizan al-Hikmah*, *al-karam*, h.60).
**Authenticity.** **Chainless.** ⚠ **Already audited in `lecture-15-audit.md`**, where it was listed among nine *Ghurar*/*'Uyun* citations carrying **no isnad at all**.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified — text located and stable; ungradeable.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ He quotes it correctly and, to his credit, flags it as hard to live up to. ⚠ Second appearance in two lectures without the chainless status ever being mentioned. The Qur'anic anchor for the same principle — **41:34**, *idfa' bi'llati hiya ahsan* — was audited in lecture 15 and is far stronger ground; he should lead with the verse and use the maxim as illustration.

### N11. Imam al-Sadiq on ﴾wa qulu li'l-nasi husna﴿ — smile fully at the believer, speak to others with *mudara* — [33:06]
**Status.** ⚠ **NOT LOCATED as a single narration** within the search budget. Its two limbs are separately attested:
- **al-Mizan on 2:83** (Arabic retrieved, see the Qur'an section) reads the verse as covering "**their disbeliever and their believer alike**" — «كناية عن حسن المعاشرة مع الناس، كافرهم ومؤمنهم» — which is exactly the two-tier scope he claims.
- The al-Kafi gloss that al-Mizan actually cites from **Imam al-Sadiq** on this verse is «قُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَقُولُوا إِلَّا خَيْراً حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا هُوَ» — say nothing but good until you know what it is. That is a different (and narrower) gloss.
- The vocabulary he uses — *fa-yabsutu lahum wajhah* / *fa-yukallimuhum bi'l-mudarat* — belongs to the *taqiyya wa mudara* narration family (al-Kafi 2:117 ff.; Bihar ch. 73), where the distinction between dealing with *mu'minin* and with *mukhalifin* is genuinely made.
**Verdict.** ⚠ **Substance defensible, specific attribution unverified.** He should either cite al-Mizan on 2:83 (which says what he wants, plainly, and is easy for a parent to check) or locate the narration properly. Do not repeat "Imam al-Sadiq said this about the verse" with the *yabsutu wajhah* wording until it is pinned.
**Confidence.** NOT LOCATED (limited search).

### N12. "Islam began as a stranger and will return as a stranger" — [25:00]
**Arabic.** «بَدَأَ الإِسْلَامُ غَرِيباً وَسَيَعُودُ غَرِيباً كَمَا بَدَأَ، فَطُوبَى لِلْغُرَبَاءِ»
**Reference.** ⚠ **Sunni-canonical: Sahih Muslim 145** (Kitab al-Iman), also Ibn Majah 3986, Tirmidhi 2629, Ahmad. **Sahih.**
**Imami transmission.** **NOT LOCATED** in an Imami primary collection within this audit's budget (one search). It circulates widely in Shia preaching and appears in later Imami anthologies, but no al-Kafi / al-Saduq / al-Tusi placement was confirmed.
**Confidence.** Strongly verified as **Sunni**; **needs further verification** as Imami.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ The content and the application (hold your principles when they look strange) are sound and the wording is right. ⚠ He introduces it as "the Hadith tells us this" to a Shia audience without noting it is a *sahih* **Sunni** text with no confirmed Imami chain — the same pattern the index flags for *kullu mawludin yuladu 'ala'l-fitrah*, *la yuldaghu al-mu'min*, and *al-mar'u 'ala dini khalilih*. **This is now a recurring habit across the series and worth naming as such.**

### N13. "There is no monasticism in Islam" — [23:00]
**Status.** ⚠ He does not quote it; he says "we don't have any idea of a hadith about being a monk." **As a standalone hadith, «لا رهبانية في الإسلام» is not established** — the attested forms are «إنَّ مِن سُنَّتي النِّكاحَ… ولا رَهبانِيَّةَ في الإسلامِ» and «لا رَهبانِيَّةَ ولا تَبَتُّلَ في الإسلامِ», both weak in the Sunni takhrij literature (discussed as such by al-Lajna al-Da'ima).
**Better Imami substitute.** The Prophet to **'Uthman b. Maz'un**: «لَمْ يَبْعَثْنِي اللَّهُ بِالرَّهْبَانِيَّةِ، وَلَكِنْ بَعَثَنِي بِالحَنِيفِيَّةِ السَّهْلَةِ السَّمْحَةِ» — **al-Kafi 5:494**, Kitab al-Nikah. Same point, real chain, Imami.
**Verdict.** ✅ His theological claim is correct; ⚠ the slogan he half-quotes is not the strong text. Use al-Kafi 5:494.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified.

### N14. ⭐ Imam al-Kazim and the man with the farm outside Medina — [35:08]
**What the sources say.** The man is **a descendant of 'Umar b. al-Khattab** living in Medina, who used to harass the Imam and insult 'Ali b. Abi Talib. The Imam's companions asked permission to kill him; he forbade it, asked where the man was, and rode out to his **farm outside Medina** on his mule. The man shouted «لا تُوطِئْ زَرْعَنَا» — *don't trample our crop* — and the Imam rode straight through it, sat with him, joked with him, then asked: «كَمْ غَرِمْتَ فِي زَرْعِكَ هَذَا؟» — *how much did you spend on this crop?* — **"a hundred dinars"**; «وَكَمْ تَرْجُو أَنْ تُصِيبَ؟» — **"I hope for two hundred"**; whereupon the Imam produced a purse of **three hundred dinars** and gave it to him. The man later stood in the mosque praising the Imam («اللهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَتَهُ»), was mocked by his former friends, and defended his new position. The Imam then turned to the companions who had wanted to kill him and asked: «**أَيُّمَا كَانَ خَيْراً، مَا أَرَدْتُمْ أَوْ مَا أَرَدْتُ؟**» — *which was better, what you wanted or what I wanted?*
**Reference.** **Abu'l-Faraj al-Isfahani, *Maqatil al-Talibiyyin*, pp. 499-500**; **al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, *Tarikh Baghdad* 13:28**; and **al-Shaykh al-Mufid, *al-Irshad*** (life of Imam al-Kazim).
**Chain.** A 4th-century AH historical report with a chain in *Maqatil*; not a *hadith* in a fiqh collection. ⭐ Notably **cross-attested in a Sunni source** (*Tarikh Baghdad*), which strengthens it considerably as history.
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified.**
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Substantially accurate and well chosen** — including the detail about riding over the crop, the joking, the purse, and the closing question, which he gets right and which is the whole point of the story. ⚠ **Two corrections.** (1) The man hoped for **200** dinars, not 300; the Imam gave **300**, i.e. **more than the man hoped for**, which is a stronger version of the speaker's own moral than the one he tells. (2) He adds "Allah gives us *rizq* based on what we hope for" as the Imam's line; that sentence is **not in the source** — it is the speaker's gloss.

### N15. Amir al-Mu'minin: amazed at the man who withholds a favour he could give — [38:09]
**Arabic.** «عَجِبْتُ لِرَجُلٍ يَأْتِيهِ أَخُوهُ المُسْلِمُ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَيَمْتَنِعُ عَنْ قَضَائِهَا، وَلَا يَرَى نَفْسَهُ لِلْخَيْرِ أَهْلاً»
**Translation.** "I marvel at a man whose Muslim brother comes to him with a need and he refuses to meet it, not seeing himself as fit for good."
**Reference.** Imam Ali, ***Ghurar al-Hikam*** (via Rayshahri, *Mizan al-Hikmah*, *qada' al-hawa'ij*).
**Authenticity.** **Chainless.** *Ghurar* carries no isnad.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified.
**Verdict.** ✅ Wording and sense accurate; the speaker's paraphrase ("he doesn't consider himself worthy of *khayr*") is exactly right and is the interesting part of the saying.

### N16. ⭐ The continuation: "even if we hoped for no paradise and feared no fire" — [39:09]
**Arabic.** «لَوْ كُنَّا لَا نَرْجُو جَنَّةً وَلَا نَخْشَى نَاراً وَلَا ثَوَاباً وَلَا عِقَاباً، لَكَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نَطْلُبَ مَكَارِمَ الأَخْلَاقِ»
**Translation.** "Even if we hoped for no paradise and feared no fire, and there were neither reward nor punishment, it would still behove us to seek out nobility of character."
**Reference.** Imam Ali — **al-Nuri al-Tabarsi, *Mustadrak al-Wasa'il* 11:193**. (A widely circulated variant attributes it to the Prophet.)
**Authenticity.** *Mustadrak* is a supplement of reports **al-Hurr al-'Amili excluded from Wasa'il**, largely for weakness of source; this one carries no chain. **Ungradeable / weak by provenance.**
**Confidence.** **Moderately verified** — text and attribution located, source late and chainless.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ⚠ **He presents N15 and N16 as one continuous narration ("Then comes the Imam's part…").** They are **two separate sayings** from two different compilations. The theological point he draws — that the drive to serve is native to the *fitrah* and not merely reward-driven — is genuinely in N16 and is a fine point; but he should not weld them.

### N17. ⭐ Imam al-Sajjad, the indebted man, the two loaves, the fish and the two pearls — [41:10]-[45:12]
**What the source actually says.** A man came to **Ali b. al-Husayn (al-Sajjad)** complaining of heavy debt (the figure given is **four hundred dinars**) and a large family. The Imam **wept**. Asked why, he said tears are for real calamity — and what calamity is greater than seeing a believer in need one cannot relieve? He then called for the household's food, and there were **two loaves (قرصتان)** of coarse bread, the Imam's own *suhur* and *iftar*. He gave them to the man. The man traded one loaf for a fish and the other for salt; on gutting the fish he found **two pearls**. The **fish-seller** and then the **salt-seller** came back, each unable to eat the bread and returning it. Then a messenger came **from Imam al-Sajjad himself**, saying: return our food to us — this is food only we eat; Allah used it to relieve you.
**Reference.** **Shaykh 'Abbas al-Qummi, *Muntaha al-Amal fi Tawarikh al-Nabi wa'l-Al*, vol. 2, pp. 38-39**, in the *mu'jizat* material for Imam al-Sajjad. Earlier placement in the *manaqib*/*kharaij* literature and Bihar vol. 46 is likely but **could not be pinned within budget**.
**Chain.** None reproduced. It is a *mu'jizah* narrative in a late (early-20th-century) compilation.
**Authenticity.** **No grading exists.** *Muntaha al-Amal* is a devotional history, not a *hadith* collection with chains.
**Confidence.** **Moderately verified** — the story is located and its shape matches the speaker's telling closely.
**⭐ VERDICT ON THE SPEAKER'S KEY ERROR.** The captions have him say the recall messenger came **"from Imam Sadiq."** ❌ **That is wrong.** In the source the story is **Imam al-Sajjad's throughout** — he weeps, he sends the loaves, and **he** sends the messenger to recall them. There is no Imam al-Sadiq in the narrative. (This may be a slip of the tongue rather than a considered claim, but a parent retelling it will pass on the error.)
**Two further notes.** (1) The debt in the source is **400 dinars**; the speaker gives no figure. (2) The mocking-opponent episode he inserts in the middle — the man overhearing someone jeer that the Imams "say the heavens and earth are at their disposal yet cannot help their own followers" — is part of the received telling and functions as the trigger for the Imam's "now the time has come."
**Practical meaning.** ✅ The lesson he draws is exactly the source's own: the Imam's *empathy* preceded and did not depend on his *means*. That is worth teaching, and the weak provenance does not damage it because the empathy half — the weeping and the "what calamity is greater" line — is the part that carries the moral, not the miracle.

### N18. ⭐ "Shall I not tell you of the noblest traits?" — the *muwasat* hadith — [46:14]
**Arabic.** «أَلَا أُحَدِّثُكَ بِمَكَارِمِ الأَخْلَاقِ؟ الصَّفْحُ عَنِ النَّاسِ، وَمُوَاسَاةُ الرَّجُلِ أَخَاهُ فِي مَالِهِ، وَذِكْرُ اللهِ كَثِيراً»
**Translation.** "Shall I not tell you of the noble traits? Pardoning people; a man's sharing with his brother from his wealth; and remembering Allah abundantly."
**Reference.** Imam al-Sadiq — **al-Hurr al-'Amili, *Wasa'il al-Shi'a* (Al al-Bayt edn.) 15:200**, drawn from the al-Kafi *makarim al-akhlaq* material.
**Chain.** Wasa'il transmits al-Kafi's chain; no rijal verdict retrieved.
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified** as to text, attribution and reference; grading unretrieved.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Accurate on all three items and in the right order** — forgiveness, *muwasat* with wealth, abundant *dhikr*. He renders *safh* as "forgive people," which is right. ⚠ Note for the parent: this is a **three-item** list and *dhikr* is the third — a lecture on *muwasat* that quotes this hadith and then drops the *dhikr* clause has quoted two-thirds of it.
**Practical meaning.** *Muwasat* is not *sadaqa*. It is **sharing from what you have as an equal**, not giving down from surplus; the verb governs *akhahu fi malihi* — his brother, in his own wealth. The speaker's gloss ("it doesn't mean giving condolences") is a genuinely useful correction of a common Urdu/Arabic false friend.

### N19. ⭐ Imam al-Sadiq: test the Shia at three points — [47:14]
**Arabic.** «امْتَحِنُوا شِيعَتَنَا عِنْدَ ثَلَاثٍ: عِنْدَ مَوَاقِيتِ الصَّلَاةِ كَيْفَ مُحَافَظَتُهُمْ عَلَيْهَا، وَعِنْدَ أَسْرَارِهِمْ كَيْفَ حِفْظُهُمْ لَهَا عِنْدَ عَدُوِّنَا، وَإِلَى أَمْوَالِهِمْ كَيْفَ مُوَاسَاتُهُمْ لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ فِيهَا»
**Translation.** "Test our Shia at three points: at the times of prayer, how they guard them; at their secrets, how they keep them from our enemy; and at their wealth, how they share it with their brothers."
**Reference.** **al-Shaykh al-Saduq, *al-Khisal*, p. 103, h. 62**, from Imam al-Sadiq. A **two-item** variant is also transmitted, from al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar: «اخْتَبِرْ شِيعَتَنَا فِي خَصْلَتَيْنِ: المُحَافَظَةِ عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ فِي مَوَاقِيتِهِنَّ، وَالمُوَاسَاةِ لِلْإِخْوَانِ» (in Bihar's *bab muwasat al-ikhwan*, h.8).
**Chain.** *al-Khisal* gives isnads; no rijal verdict on this specific chain retrieved.
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified** — text, three items, order, Imam and reference all confirmed.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Fully accurate.** He gets all three, in order, with the right emphasis on the third (*muwasat*) and the correct framing of the second (secrets **before the enemy**, not secrets in general). One of the two best citations in the lecture.
**Practical meaning.** Worth telling a parent that the two-item variant exists and drops the secrets clause — the constant across both versions is **prayer on time + sharing wealth**.

### N20. ⭐ Imam al-Baqir: "they are not the Shia" — [47:14]
**Arabic.** «فَهَلْ يَعْطِفُ الغَنِيُّ عَلَى الفَقِيرِ؟ وَهَلْ يَتَجَاوَزُ المُحْسِنُ عَنِ المُسِيءِ؟ وَيَتَوَاسَوْنَ؟ فَقُلْتُ: لَا. فَقَالَ: **لَيْسَ هَؤُلَاءِ شِيعَةً، الشِّيعَةُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ هَذَا**»
**Translation.** "'Does the rich among them incline to the poor? Does the one who does good overlook the one who wrongs him? And do they practise *muwasat*?' I said: no. He said: **these are not Shia. The Shia are those who do this.**"
**Reference.** Narrated by **Abu Isma'il** from **Abu Ja'far al-Baqir**; reproduced in Bihar's *bab muwasat al-ikhwan* (h.94). The original is in **al-Kafi**, Kitab al-Iman wa'l-Kufr, in the *haqq al-mu'min* / *muwasat* material (2:173 in the common pagination) — ⚠ the exact al-Kafi hadith number was **not pinned** within budget.
**Chain.** Abu Isma'il ← al-Baqir; no grading retrieved.
**Confidence.** **Strongly verified** as to text and content; **moderately** as to precise reference.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Accurate, including the three questions and the sting in the reply.** He renders the second question ("if somebody is mistreated, do they forgive the one who mistreated them") correctly — note it is the *muhsin* overlooking the *musi'*, i.e. the same "higher path" principle as N10, which makes his structure coherent.
**Practical meaning.** The full narration opens with the man boasting of the number of Shia in Kufa; the Imam's reply defines Shi'ism by **conduct**, not census. That framing is the whole point and the speaker gets it.

### N21. "The *karim* rejoices in his bounty; the base man boasts of his possessions" — [61:27]
**Arabic.** «إِنَّ الكَرِيمَ يَبْتَهِجُ بِفَضْلِهِ، وَاللَّئِيمَ يَفْتَخِرُ بِمُلْكِهِ»
**Reference.** ⚠ Attributed in the maxim collections to **Imam Zayn al-'Abidin (al-Sajjad)** (Rayshahri, *Mizan al-Hikmah*, *al-karam*, h.22) — **not** left unattributed, and not Imam Ali.
**Authenticity.** Chainless maxim corpus.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified.
**Verdict.** ✅ Wording accurate (the captions' "yabta hijub faliha" = *yabtahiju bi-fadlihi*). ⚠ The contrast in the Arabic is *fadl* (bounty given) vs *mulk* (possession held) — the speaker renders the second half as "they take pride in their possessions," which is right. He should name Imam al-Sajjad: it dovetails with his own Imam al-Sajjad material.

### N22. The *karim* and the *la'im* on debts of kindness — [59:24]
**Arabic.** «الكَرِيمُ يَرَى مَكَارِمَ أَفْعَالِهِ دَيْناً عَلَيْهِ يَقْضِيهِ، وَاللَّئِيمُ يَرَى سَوَالِفَ إِحْسَانِهِ دَيْناً لَهُ يَقْتَضِيهِ»
**Translation.** "The noble man sees his own noble acts as a debt **upon** him, which he discharges; the base man sees his past kindnesses as a debt **owed to** him, which he collects."
**Reference.** **Imam Ali, *Ghurar al-Hikam*** (Rayshahri, *al-karam*, h.32) — the two clauses are **one saying**, not two.
**Authenticity.** Chainless.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **He gets the grammatical hinge exactly right**, which is the hard part: *daynan **'alayhi** yaqdi* vs *daynan **lahu** yaqtadi* — the same word *dayn*, flipped by one preposition, and two different verbs from the same root (*qada* = to pay off, *iqtada* = to exact payment). His parenting application (the child who feels indebted vs the child who keeps a tab) is a legitimate extension, not something the maxim says on its own.

### N23. "The base man is the one who is constantly reminding you of his favours" — [60:26]
**Arabic.** «الكَرِيمُ مَنْ بَذَلَ إِحْسَانَهُ، اللَّئِيمُ مَنْ كَثُرَ امْتِنَانُهُ»
**Reference.** **Imam Ali, *Ghurar al-Hikam*** (Rayshahri, *al-karam*, h.27).
**Authenticity.** Chainless.
**Confidence.** Moderately verified.
**Verdict.** ✅ The half he quotes (*man kathura imtinanuh*) is accurate. ⚠ He drops the first half, which is the definition the second half contrasts with. *Imtinan* here = the reproachful reminding the Qur'an calls **al-mann** (2:264) — worth pairing, and it would give him a verse for the point.

### N24. Imam al-Husayn: people's needs are a blessing upon you — [62:28]
**Arabic.** «اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ حَوَائِجَ النَّاسِ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ نِعَمِ اللهِ عَلَيْكُمْ، فَلَا تَمَلُّوا النِّعَمَ فَتَتَحَوَّلَ إِلَى غَيْرِكُمْ» (a common variant ends «فَتَحُورَ نِقَماً» — "lest they turn into afflictions").
**Translation.** "Know that people's needs of you are among Allah's blessings upon you; so do not weary of the blessings, lest they be transferred to someone else."
**Reference.** Imam al-Husayn — **Bihar al-Anwar 75:127** (his *mawa'iz*). The same passage continues with «مَنْ نَفَّسَ كُرْبَةَ مُؤْمِنٍ فَرَّجَ اللهُ عَنْهُ كُرَبَ الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ».
**Chain.** Bihar's *mawa'iz* material for al-Husayn is largely drawn from *Tuhaf al-'Uqul*-type sources — **chainless**.
**Confidence.** **Moderately verified** — wording, attribution and Bihar reference confirmed.
**Verdict on the speaker's use.** ✅ **Accurate, including the ending he gives** ("Allah remove them from you and give them to somebody else" = *fa-tatahawwala ila ghayrikum*). A good closing citation, correctly rendered.

## Named individuals and narrative material

### Shaheed Muhammad Boroujerdi — [13:49]-[18:56]
**Identification.** ✅ **Correct and unambiguous: Shahid Mohammad Boroujerdi (محمد بروجردی)**, IRGC commander in Kurdistan, popularly titled ***Masih-e Kordestan*** ("the Christ of Kurdistan") for his conciliatory dealings with the Kurdish population.
**Verified facts.** Born **1955**; killed **22 May 1983** by a landmine on the **Mahabad–Naqadeh road** in Kurdistan; **28** by Gregorian reckoning (Persian sources commonly say 29 in solar years — the speaker's "29, not even 30" is within the normal Iranian usage). He commanded the IRGC ground forces in Kurdistan and later its seventh zone across several western provinces.
**The SAVAK episode.** ⚠ **Partially corroborated, not as told.** Boroujerdi's documented pre-revolutionary record includes desertion from conscription, capture and six months' detention by SAVAK with beatings, then clandestine work reproducing Khomeini's statements and cassettes, and armed guerrilla activity from January 1978. **The specific story — borrowing a revolver that jams, then killing a SAVAK agent by pistol-whipping him — is NOT LOCATED (limited search)** in any accessible source. Do not repeat it as established.
**The truck driver and the slap.** ⚠ **Attested as a story about him, unverified in detail.** An Iranian news feature is published under the headline «ماجرای سیلی سرباز بر صورت فرمانده / مسیح کردستان لقب چه کسی بود؟» ("the story of the slap on the commander's face / whose title was 'Christ of Kurdistan'?"), which confirms that a slap anecdote circulates about Boroujerdi. **The page itself was 403-blocked at the egress proxy**, so the details the speaker gives — the narrator being "Montazeri", the driver from **Sanandaj**, the later scene in the commander's office and the priority delivery — could not be checked. ⚠ Note also that the speaker's version has the slap happen *on the road* and the office scene *the same evening*; the headline's framing is "a soldier's slap," which may be a different setting.
**Narrator "Montazeri".** **NOT IDENTIFIED.** Several revolutionary figures bear the name; nothing in the accessible record ties one of them to this anecdote.
**Verdict.** ✅ The man is real, correctly named, correctly placed and roughly correctly aged. ⚠ **Both anecdotes should be told as "it is related that…", not as documented history.** The one that carries the lesson (the slap) is at least attested as circulating about him; the one that does not (the pistol-whipping) is not.

### Shahida "Sayyida Fahida / Tahira Hashimi" — [48:17]-[50:20]
**Identification.** ✅ Almost certainly **Shahideh Sayyideh Tahereh Hashemi (شهیده سیّده طاهره هاشمی)** — the captions' "Fahida" then "Tahira" resolve to *Tahereh*. She is listed among the **martyrs of the *Hemaseh-ye Amol*** (the Amol uprising, Mazandaran, 6 Bahman 1360 / late January 1982), and has dedicated Persian memorial pages and a provincial-government biography.
**The two specific claims.** ⚠ **NOT VERIFIED.** (a) That **Shahid Beheshti** told her at **14** that she would die a martyr; (b) that she secretly spent her allowance on classmates' backpacks, shoes and school materials, discovered only when friends came to her funeral. Every Persian source carrying her biography — habilian.ir, ostan-mz.ir, mehrnews.com, the memorial blogs — was **403-blocked or robots-blocked at the egress proxy**. This is an **unreachable-archive negative, not a completed negative search**: the claims may well be documented in exactly those pages.
**Chronology check.** ✅ **Internally consistent.** Beheshti was killed 28 June 1981; the Amol uprising was January 1982. A meeting between them before mid-1981 is perfectly possible.
**Verdict.** ✅ The person is real and correctly identified. ⚠ Present the two anecdotes as *narrated by her family*, which is how he frames them — that framing is honest and should be kept.

### Shaheed Mahdi Bakeri — [54:22]
**Identification.** ✅ **Shahid Mehdi Bakeri (مهدی باکری)**, born **1954**, commander of the **31st Ashura Division**, killed **16 March 1985** near **al-Qurna, Iraq**, during **Operation Badr**, aged **31**. His body was never recovered: the boat carrying him was hit by an RPG and sank in the Tigris. He is the **brother of Shahid Hamid Bakeri**, already covered in `_verified-index.md` (Hamid: martyred 25 February 1984, Operation Khaybar; his body also never recovered).
**The speaker's "around 30 when he dies."** ✅ Close enough — 31.
**The water-container anecdote.** ⚠ **NOT LOCATED (limited search).** The story — Bakeri seen alone before Fajr filling *aftabeh* (water jugs) and arranging them in front of the latrine stalls for the other fighters, narrated by a radio-communications soldier stationed near the command post — is exactly the register of the *"100 khaterat az Shahid Mehdi Bakeri"* memoir literature, and Persian collections of his humility anecdotes exist. **Every Iranian site carrying them (aviny.com, mashreghnews.ir, defapress.ir) was robots-blocked at the egress proxy.** Unverified rather than refuted.
**Verdict.** ✅ Person correctly identified and dated. ⚠ Anecdote unverified; tell it as memoir, not record. ✅ The speaker's use of it — humility and joy in unseen service as the mark of the *karim* — matches the man's documented reputation.

### Sayyid Ali Jafri, podcast "Sweeter Than Honey" — [01:38]
**Status.** ⚠ **NOT LOCATED (limited search).** No podcast of that name by a Sayyid Ali Jafri surfaced.
**What the title alludes to.** ✅ Worth knowing: the phrase is **Qasim b. al-Hasan's** at Karbala, when his uncle al-Husayn asked how he found death — «**يَا عَمِّ، المَوْتُ أَحْلَى عِنْدِي مِنَ العَسَلِ**», "uncle, death is sweeter to me than honey." It is in **Ibn Tawus, *al-Luhuf*** and thence **Bihar al-Anwar vol. 45** — *maqtal* material, **chainless**. Qasim's traditional age at Karbala is around 13-14, which is exactly why the speaker ties it to "when they're 14."
**Verdict.** ✅ The allusion is apt and correctly aimed. ⚠ The podcast itself is unverified; and a parent should know the source phrase is *maqtal* literature without a chain.

## Non-scripture claims

| Claim | Timestamp | Status |
|---|---|---|
| *Mudara* is best rendered "Islamic tolerance" | 19:57 | ⚠ **Defensible but loose.** Lexically *mudara* is amicable, conciliatory handling of people — *daraa* = to ward off gently. "Tolerance" imports a modern political sense. Bihar files it under ***taqiyya***, and the qualifier in the corpus is «**في غير ترك حقّ**» (Bihar 74:145) — without abandoning a right. His own four-option framing (isolation / permanent war / chameleon / principled flexibility) is his construction, not a classical taxonomy, and he says so implicitly by calling them "scenarios we're going to explore" |
| The four *mudara* goals by age 14 (swallow anger, good *akhlaq*, no *hiqd*, walk the higher path) | 20:57 | ⚠ **The speaker's own rubric.** No classical text enumerates them. Each element is separately sourceable (*kazm al-ghayz* Q 3:134; *hiqd* in the *Ghurar* corpus; *ihsan* for *isa'ah* = N10 / Q 41:34) but the set and the age-14 marker are his |
| "Sara" and "Awesome/Aasim & Najma" case studies | 27:02, 55:22 | ✅ **Explicitly presented as illustrative fiction** ("we've changed his name"). No verification issue. Note they are the pedagogical style of Jam'iyyat al-Ma'arif's *al-Walad al-Salih*, the series' identified curriculum |
| "The book that we're going through" with the picture of the child giving his coat away | 40:10 | ⚠ Unnamed. Consistent with the curriculum identified in `_verified-index.md` (**Jam'iyyat al-Ma'arif al-Islamiyya al-Thaqafiyya, *al-Walad al-Salih* / *al-Tarbiya bi'l-Hubb***). Naming the book aloud would let parents buy it |
| "Raising the elite soldiers of Imam Mahdi" | 06:44 | ⚠ Already in `_verified-index.md`: **homiletic**. Nearest text is al-Nu'mani, *al-Ghayba* bab 20 h.10 («إن أصحاب القائم شباب لا كهول فيهم») — weak chain, no published grading |
| *Karamah* precedes and produces *taqwa* | 07:44 onwards | ✅ Already settled in `_verified-index.md`: the classical anchor is **Nahj al-Balagha, Hikmah 449** — «مَنْ كَرُمَتْ عَلَيْهِ نَفْسُهُ هَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ شَهْوَتُهُ» (chainless), with **al-Mizan on 17:70** for *karamah* as **intrinsic**, not comparative. The framework is sound; the sourcing is chainless |
| The recap list of *karim* traits (moral compass, *dunya* insignificant, avoids sin, truthful, no foul language, guards the gaze, *ghayrah*, keeps trusts and secrets, controls anger, forgives) | 08:44-11:48 | ⚠ **Recap of Parts 14-15.** The *ghayrah* limb (*ghayrat al-mar'ah kufr wa ghayrat al-rajul iman*) and the trust/secrets limb were audited in `lecture-15-audit.md`: **nine of that lecture's citations are chainless *Ghurar*/*'Uyun al-Hikam*, and four were absence-checked against the al-Kafi chapters that should contain them and are not there.** The *ghayrah* restriction has a real basis he never cites — **al-Kafi 5, Kitab al-Nikah, ch.178**, «لا غَيْرَةَ فِي الْحَلَالِ» |
| "Good guys finish last" / "will people think I'm a chump?" | 12:49 | ✅ Handled honestly — he raises the objection, defers the exceptions, and asks the audience to establish the principle first. Note **Q 41:34** (audited in lecture 15) contains the answer he defers: *idfa' bi'llati hiya ahsan* is framed there as strategically effective, not merely pious |

## Better-sourced substitutes

1. **For "the best legacy is a righteous child"** → **al-Kafi 7:57**: «سِتَّةٌ تَلْحَقُ المُؤْمِنَ بَعْدَ وَفَاتِهِ: وَلَدٌ يَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُ، وَمُصْحَفٌ يُخَلِّفُهُ، وَغَرْسٌ يَغْرِسُهُ، وَقَلِيبٌ يَحْفِرُهُ، وَصَدَقَةٌ يُجْرِيهَا، وَسُنَّةٌ يُؤْخَذُ بِهَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ». It contains his own improvised list (wells, charity, practice) **and** the righteous child, in an Imami primary, and here the child comes first.
2. **For the "meet bad with good" litmus test** → lead with **Q 41:34** (audited in `lecture-15-audit.md`) and keep the *Ghurar* maxim as illustration, not as proof.
3. **For "Islam began as a stranger"** → say plainly that it is **Sahih Muslim 145**. If an Imami text is wanted for the same point, **al-Kafi 2:242** *bab fi qillat 'adad al-mu'minin* material serves.
4. **For "no monasticism"** → **al-Kafi 5:494**: «لَمْ يَبْعَثْنِي اللهُ بِالرَّهْبَانِيَّةِ، وَلَكِنْ بَعَثَنِي بِالحَنِيفِيَّةِ السَّهْلَةِ السَّمْحَةِ».
5. **For the "*mudara* without limits" worry** → quote the qualifier that is in the same corpus: «رَأْسُ العَقْلِ بَعْدَ الإِيمَانِ بِاللهِ مُدَارَاةُ النَّاسِ **فِي غَيْرِ تَرْكِ حَقٍّ**» (Bihar 74:145). It answers the "am I a chump?" objection from inside the tradition.
6. **For "*man kathura imtinanuhu*"** → pair with **Q 2:264**, «لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُم بِالْمَنِّ وَالأَذَىٰ», which gives a Qur'anic anchor to the whole *la'im* discussion.
7. **For the *karamah* framework as a whole** → **Nahj al-Balagha Hikmah 449** + **al-Mizan on 17:70** (both already in `_verified-index.md`) remain the right classical anchors, and neither was cited in this lecture.
